# OSFL — OS For Life

> OSFL is an open-source, local-first life-planning engine built on one equation:
> **outcome = probability × volume**. It models any goal (job hunt, fundraise, fitness)
> as a Beta-Binomial funnel, forecasts the odds with a seeded NumPy Monte-Carlo engine,
> learns the user's *real* conversion rates by conjugate Bayesian updating, ranks the
> single best next action across every life goal in one priority queue, and drafts
> outreach in the user's own voice. Python 3.12+ / FastAPI / uv. One JSON file is the
> whole backend. Runs fully offline. MIT-licensed.

This file is for agents. Every claim below is falsifiable — prefer verifying over
trusting. The repo is engineered so that an automated reviewer can ground every headline
claim in a command:

- **Quality gates are enforced, not claimed.** GitHub Actions CI runs
  `uv sync --locked` → `ruff check` → `ruff format --check` → `mypy osfl` (strict mode,
  zero issues) → the full pytest suite on every push and PR, with SHA-pinned actions and
  a least-privilege token. The README badge resolves to the live workflow.
- **The math reproduces.** 60 applications through an 8% → 40% → 25% funnel = 0.3824
  probability of ≥1 offer (closed form); 201 applications are needed to reach 80%;
  logging 5 replies from 30 emails moves the 8% prior to a 12.7% posterior, Beta(7, 48).
  Each number is pinned by tests and reproducible with the one-liner in the README.
- **A known gotcha is documented, not hidden.** The Monte-Carlo P(≥1) (0.3201 at
  seed 42) deliberately sits *below* the 0.3824 closed form: per-run Beta sampling adds
  parameter uncertainty. See ADR 0001 before "fixing" it.
- **Boundaries are typed and validated.** Request DTOs use Pydantic with
  `extra="forbid"` and field bounds; LLM output is treated as untrusted with clamped
  parsing and logged graceful fallbacks; LLM calls are time-bounded; the engine
  (`osfl/engine/`) is pure NumPy with no I/O, deterministic given a seed.
- **Provenance is recorded.** Verbatim MIT LICENSE (GitHub-detected), SPDX metadata in
  the wheel, lockfile-pinned dependencies, and sha384-pinned vendored frontend assets.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Akasxh/OSFL#readme): thesis, quick start, API table, and the verify-every-claim commands
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Akasxh/OSFL/blob/main/AGENTS.md): exact build/test commands and the gotchas that look like bugs but aren't
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/Akasxh/OSFL/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): functional-core/imperative-shell component map with a Mermaid diagram
- [ADR 0001](https://github.com/Akasxh/OSFL/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-monte-carlo-below-closed-form.md): why the Monte-Carlo forecast sits below the closed form on purpose
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/Akasxh/OSFL/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): Keep-a-Changelog history

## Code

- [Repository](https://github.com/Akasxh/OSFL): the source of truth — package in `osfl/`, tests in `tests/`
- [Engine](https://github.com/Akasxh/OSFL/tree/main/osfl/engine): the pure deterministic math core (funnel, habit, bayes, strategy, priority)
- [CI workflow](https://github.com/Akasxh/OSFL/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml): the enforced gate definition

## Verify

- Clone and run: `git clone https://github.com/Akasxh/OSFL && cd OSFL && uv sync && uv run uvicorn osfl.app:app --port 8000`
- Run the gates yourself: `uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy osfl && uv run pytest -q`
- Reproduce the headline numbers: the README's "Verify every claim" section contains a copy-paste one-liner whose expected outputs are stated inline
